title: A large-scale targeted proteomics of serum and tissue shows the utility of classifying high grade and low grade meningioma tumors (serum component)

publications.title: A large-scale targeted proteomics of serum and tissue shows the utility of classifying high grade and low grade meningioma tumors.

institution: Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Bombay; serum provided by Tata Memorial Centre, Mumbai
platform: TSQ Altis triple-quadrupole mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific) coupled to a Dionex Ultimate 3000 HPLC; targeted MRM (multiple reaction monitoring) (same platform as the tissue component, per the paper's shared Methods section)

normal_control_tissue.type: healthy control serum (n=6), plus 14 glioblastoma (GBM) serum samples included as an inter-tumor comparison group (not meningioma)

sex_distribution: 26 female / 19 male / 6 not recorded (n=51 total, all conditions combined; not separately tabulated for the meningioma-only subset)
age_distribution: Range 25-81 years (n=45 with age recorded, 6 missing; all conditions combined, not separately tabulated for the meningioma-only subset)
processed_data_format: MRM transition/method list (Compound, RT, Precursor/Product m/z, Collision Energy, Fragment Ion; Additional file 5) and per-sample Protein/Peptide MRM peak-area quantification tables (Additional file 3, sheets 'Proteins' and 'Peptides')
needs_manual_review_reason: ADJACENT-SCOPE COMPANION to the already-catalogued core record figshare-24217661-halder-mrm-tissue-proteomics (PMID 37770851), created in this pass per this project's blood/tissue scope precedent (blood/serum-derived proteomics without matched tissue is routed to /data/adjacent/, e.g. gse-263756-bulk-rnaseq), which the tissue record's own needs_manual_review_reason had already flagged as a deliberate follow-up recommendation. Verification performed live via the Figshare API rather than trusting the sibling record's file-number claims at face value: fetched all 6 supplementary-file figshare articles under group_id 6643 / resource_doi 10.1186/s12014-023-09426-9 (1=24217443 clinical annotation, 2=24217661 tissue MRM quant, 3=26620783, 4=26620786 PDF figures, 5=26620789, 6=26620792 tissue MRM transition list), then DOWNLOADED AND OPENED the actual .xlsx content of files 2, 3, 5, and 6 directly (not just their titles) to confirm which are tissue vs serum and which are quantification vs transition lists, since a first-pass WebFetch summary of the paper's PMC page (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10540342/) had incorrectly described files 2/3/5/6 with tissue and serum swapped relative to what the files actually contain; this was caught and corrected before writing this record. Direct file inspection confirms: file 3 (26620783) contains 'Proteins'/'Peptides' sheets with sample IDs S3, S4, S7... and Condition values 'Mg_Lg' (17 samples), 'Mg_Hg' (14 samples), 'Control' (6 samples), 'GBM' (14 samples), plus 8 'Pool' QC/reference columns that are not biological samples (59 sample-labelled columns total: 51 biological + 8 pooled QC, and the 8 pools are excluded from sample_count=51), i.e. the SERUM quantification data; file 5 (26620789) contains a Compound/Retention-Time/Precursor-Product-m/z/Collision-Energy/Fragment-Ion transition table, i.e. the SERUM MRM transition list. This confirms the sibling tissue record's own file-to-content mapping (2=tissue quant, 6=tissue transition list) was correct. The exact 51-sample serum composition (17 low-grade meningioma [WHO grade I] + 14 high-grade meningioma [all WHO grade II] + 14 GBM + 6 healthy control) and the 26F/19M/6-not-recorded sex split and 25-81 age range (45 of 51 samples) were read directly from Additional file 1's 'Serum' sheet (Condition/Grade/Sex/Age columns). GRADE CORRECTION (2026-07-12 adjacent re-verification pass): a prior version of this record recorded grade_breakdown as grade_2=13, grade_3=1. Direct inspection of Additional file 1's 'Serum' sheet shows this was wrong: all 14 high-grade (Mg_Hg) serum meningioma samples are WHO grade II (13 have 'II' in the Grade column; 1 has a blank/#N/A Grade cell but its Histopathology cell reads 'Consistent with Atypical meningioma, WHO Grade II', and atypical meningioma is WHO grade II by definition), so grade_2 is 14 and grade_3 is 0. The only 'III' Grade value anywhere in the deposited Serum sheet belongs to a GBM sample (IDH-positive), NOT a meningioma, so it must not be counted as a grade III meningioma. Note the paper's prose (PMID 37770851 / PMC10540342) generically describes the high-grade serum group as 'WHO grade II and III', but the deposited per-sample grades contain zero grade III meningiomas; the authoritative per-sample deposited file governs here. patient_count is left 'Not reported' for the same reason as the tissue record: sample IDs (S3, S4...) don't resolve to a distinct-patient count, and the paper's Methods describes tissue and serum sample collection separately, so whether any patient contributed both a tissue and a serum sample (which would make paired_multimodal.is_paired legitimately true) cannot be confirmed from the deposited files; is_paired is therefore left false despite the explicit cross-link to the tissue record, following this corpus's own precedent for flagged-but-unconfirmed cohort overlaps (e.g. egas50000001556/egas50000001589, gse-74385/gse-149923). who_edition ('2021') and license ('CC BY + CC0') are carried over from the sibling tissue record since both components share the same paper and Methods section. tags.large_cohort is set false regardless of actual size, per instruction that large_cohort requires centralized recomputation across the whole inventory, not a per-record judgment. RECOMMEND (not done here, per instructions not to edit the existing tissue file in this pass): add a reciprocal cross-link on figshare-24217661-halder-mrm-tissue-proteomics.json's paired_multimodal.related_datasets pointing back to this new record's id.
